# Glossary placeholder bookmarks

Original OPC/XML fixture generated by `tools/glossary_bookmark_fixture.py`.
No third-party document or artwork is included. Five persistent rich-text
controls cover a whole prompt, a partial range, a zero-width bookmark, a shared
glossary definition, and nested ranges spanning two prompt paragraphs. The
document initially contains a bookmark whose name collides with the first prompt.
Glossary parts declare the `bbPlcHdr` type.

`tools/record_glossary_bookmark_ranges.ps1` opens this source read-only in the
reference application and records fifteen sequential edits: clear all five
values, replace all five prompts, then clear all five values again. It closes
the modified in-memory document without saving. The JSON records the reference application build,
source SHA-256, control text/state and all document bookmark ranges after every
operation. The reference offsets include structured-control boundary characters;
regressions compare text and bookmark positions relative to their owning control.

Observed in the reference application: restoring a glossary prompt copies its bookmarks
into the document; a colliding name relocates the existing bookmark. Restoring
the shared definition moves that name to the later control. Replacing a prompt
removes its contained bookmarks, including point and cross-paragraph ranges.
Clearing the value restores them again. IDs are story-local pairing identifiers;
the editor allocates unused document IDs while preserving other marker metadata.

ECMA-376 Part 1 §§17.5.2.25 and 17.5.2.39 define placeholder content/state;
§§17.13.6.1–2 define bookmark pairing and ranges. Name relocation during a prompt
editing transaction is recorded measured reference behavior, not a demonstrated
contradiction of a normative editing algorithm. Malformed markers are rejected;
table/nested-control glossary bodies and bookmark-only empty prompts remain
outside the supported editable subset.

No PDF or saved reference DOCX is asserted as evidence for these edits. Initial save
and PDF probes did not complete and were retired after the direct range capture
succeeded. Rendering is independently checked on corpus #203 against its native
the native reference PDF; this change does not alter its page rasters.
